definition: two channels generating candidates, one while I work and one while I do not

settled:
Where a candidate compact structure comes from is half conscious and half not, and both sides generate candidates.

The focused channel produces candidates while I am deliberately working the problem.

The diffuse channel produces them when I am not thinking about it at all. The clearest case is the first moment of the morning: the candidate is already there, built whole, handed over. I never watch it assemble.

The solver is the alternation rather than either channel alone. Focus loads and tests, diffuse assembles, focus comes back to check.

title: Where A Candidate Model Comes From
